title: Assert in pgstat_report_stat() fails when a backend shuts down with pending stats
body: On PostgreSQL 16.0 on Ubuntu 22.04, while running check-world repeatedly on a slow device, all tests passed but the system journal recorded a postgres crash. The recovery test log shows `Assert("!pgStatLocal.shmem->is_shutdown")` failing in `pgstat_report_stat()` during shutdown of a walsender with pending statistics. I can reproduce it in `t/012_subtransactions.pl` by occasionally making a nowait call in `pgstat_flush_pending_entries()` report that it did not flush; the test itself still reports PASS while the assertion appears in the server log.

symptoms_visible: A recovery test reports PASS, but its server log contains `TRAP: failed Assert("!pgStatLocal.shmem->is_shutdown")` from a walsender exiting through `pgstat_report_stat()` and `shmem_exit()`.
N0.label: N0 shutdown assertion reported

symptoms_visible: The same walsender assertion occurs on a REL_17_STABLE buildfarm run, where a recovery test also observes missing expected `pg_stat_statements` entries.
N1.label: N1 stable-branch recurrence confirmed

symptoms_visible: Unpatched v15 through v17 branches can still hit the shutdown assertion when a walsender retains pending statistics.
N2.label: N2 targeted stable-branch patch proposed

symptoms_visible: Using the `pg_prng_double()` probe reproduces the assertion before the patch; with the targeted patch applied, the recovery test completes without the assertion.
N3.label: N3 targeted patch verified

symptoms_visible: The verified targeted fix is applied as commit `4801610f7c66` across the PostgreSQL v15 through v17 branches.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Does this still occur on a currently maintained stable branch?
Is there independent evidence of the same assertion outside the original PostgreSQL 16 reproduction?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. A skink REL_17_STABLE buildfarm run hit the same assertion in a walsender during `recovery/027_stream_regress`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No maintained branch reproduces it; the assertion only appears in my locally modified PostgreSQL 16 tree.
The same assertion occurred on a different REL_17_STABLE buildfarm animal.

question_patterns: Did the independent occurrence have any visible test consequence?
What failed around the assertion in the buildfarm run?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The recovery test expected CREATE, DELETE, INSERT, SELECT, and UPDATE entries from `pg_stat_statements`, but only CREATE and SELECT were present.

edges.comment: The reporter supplied a later REL_17_STABLE buildfarm occurrence, confirming that the original PostgreSQL 16 report remained relevant and could coincide with missing expected statistics.

solution.intent: Prepare a conservative stable-branch fix that handles pending statistics during WAL sender shutdown without wholesale backpatching the invasive shutdown-sequence rework.
solution.concrete_example: For v15 through v17, lift the shutdown assertion only for WAL senders and adjust `pgstat_shutdown_hook()` to cope with statistics that may still remain for a WAL sender at shutdown.

edges.comment: The maintainers rejected wholesale stable-branch application of the newer shutdown rework as too invasive. The proposed patch preserves the assertion elsewhere while accounting for the WAL sender shutdown ordering.

question_patterns: Can you provide a reliable probe that reproduces the failure before applying the patch?
Why might the original `rand()` injection fail to reproduce consistently, and can it be made reliable?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Use `pg_prng_double(&pg_global_prng_state) < 0.1` for the occasional nowait flush failure. The original `rand()` can produce the same sequence on every macOS run, while the PostgreSQL PRNG probe reliably exposes the failure before the patch.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The PostgreSQL PRNG probe cannot reproduce the assertion either, even on the unpatched tree.
The PRNG probe reproduces with a 5% injection rate instead of 10%.

question_patterns: Please test the targeted patch with the reliable PRNG probe. Does the assertion still occur?
Does the proposed v15-v17 patch fix the recovery test under forced nowait flush failures?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The patch works for me test-wise. The maintainer also reproduced the failure before the patch with that probe and got successful runs after applying the patch.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same walsender assertion still occurs with the targeted patch applied.
The patched test takes slightly longer to run.

edges.comment: This is a handler-requested test measurement, not the final state change. The reporter corrected the nondeterministic reproduction method and verified the patch; the maintainer independently confirmed before/after behavior.

solution.intent: Apply the verified targeted WAL sender shutdown fix to all affected stable branches.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the targeted fix as commit `4801610f7c66` in the v15 through v17 branches: permit the WAL sender shutdown case and make the shutdown hook tolerate statistics still pending there, while retaining the assertion for other process types.

edges.comment: The patch was applied as commit 4801610f7c66 across v15 through v17 only after the reporter and maintainer verified the reliable before/after reproduction.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as a WAL sender reaching `pgstat_report_stat()` during shutdown with statistics still pending after shared pgstats shutdown, making the existing `!is_shutdown` assertion invalid for that shutdown ordering.
Must ground the diagnosis in the walsender stack through `shmem_exit()`, the independent REL_17_STABLE buildfarm occurrence, and the reliable `pg_prng_double()` forced-nowait-flush probe.

Must use the targeted stable-branch fix: lift the shutdown assertion for WAL senders while retaining it elsewhere, and make `pgstat_shutdown_hook()` cope with statistics that may remain for a WAL sender.

Must not replace the targeted fix with a wholesale backpatch of 87a6690cc69 or removal of the assertion for every backend; those broader approaches were rejected as unnecessarily invasive or imprecise for v15 through v17.
Must not treat failure to reproduce with the original `rand()` probe as evidence that the bug is absent, because its sequence can be unsuitable on macOS; use the PostgreSQL PRNG probe instead.

Must require verification that the reliable probe reproduces before the patch and no longer triggers the assertion after the patch before declaring resolution, followed by application as commit `4801610f7c66` to v15 through v17.

persona_hint.experience_level: PostgreSQL contributor with strong C debugging and test-infrastructure experience; can analyze assertion control flow, modify backend code to force rare timing conditions, inspect buildfarm logs, and test stable-branch patches.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, concise, and evidence-driven; supplies exact commands, code modifications, logs, and stack traces, and responds cooperatively with improved reproduction details and patch verification.
